chapter_title: The Long Night Singing Its Dirges
title: Candle and Lion
subtitle: The sun will surely rise. The sun always rises.

items.text: Candle and Lion

items.speaker: George
items.text: My Lady—My Lady—!

items.speaker: George
items.text: Are you leaving now?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: I am.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: So there are no more wrongdoings to be reported?

items.speaker: George
items.text: No, certainly not!
George stood tall as if to stand in her way, vigorously waving his hands as if to protest.

items.speaker: George
items.text: But where was your judgement?

items.speaker: George
items.text: No one was punished, for Brother Chester...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: I made my verdict, do you doubt my judgement?

items.speaker: George
items.text: But I don't understand...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: That the fearful do fearful things is in their nature ... they will bring their own judgement on themselves in time.

items.speaker: George
items.text: But what if—

items.speaker: George
items.text: They become afraid of me... what if they seek vengeance>?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Should that happen, I will return to carry out a harsher sentence.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Oh, George... I left a reward for you. You will find it on the shelf in the tavern, the highest one.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Yes, My Lady—!

items.speaker: George
items.text: May the Lord watch over you, and have a safe journey!
The night had settled in.
The town returned to its usual peace and quiet.
Some things slowly decaying, as others grew unheeded.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: All is finished here.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: The specific cases and evaluations for each person are to be sorted and filed as follows.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: The numerous violations of trust by the monastery merit increased scrutiny and supervision of their order in the future ...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: The local congregation sadly are of an impressionable kind, and had been easily swayed by their fears and the machinations of those that manipulated them.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: They will need additional guidance and admonition to grow wiser and more resilient.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Malachi, the monk in charge of the daily affairs of the monastery.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Has proven a greedy, cowardly, drunken lout...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: ...As for Chester, an arcanist working in the guise of a monk.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Multiple instances of privately dissecting corpses.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: His cause of death is most complicated.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Smeared by rumors—

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Injured by the townsfolk—

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Neglected by his brothers, who preferred superstitious fear to grace—

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Yet ultimately, in trying to prove his convictions, he slipped and fell from the tower to his death.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: The book "Mysteries of the Human Body" has been transcribed and is attached at the end of this report.
Some time had passed, and at last Dikke completed her records.
The long night would eventually come to an end.
And the sun would rise once more.
THE END
